## Q1 | One Workshop

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

Over the years workshops closed until The Witching Hour was the only one left selling cauldrons. The Witching Hour has a marginal cost of $MC = 10 + 2Q$. It now faces the whole market’s demand, $P = 110 - Q$, so its marginal revenue is $MR = 110 - 2Q$.

a\) What quantity maximizes the firm’s profit?

::: solution

Profit is largest where $MR = MC$: $110 - 2Q = 10 + 2Q$, so $100 = 4Q$ and $Q = 25$.

:::

b\) What price does it charge to sell that quantity?

::: solution

Go up to demand at 25 cauldrons: $P = 110 - 25 = 85$.

:::

c\) Calculate the firm’s maximal profit if $ATC = 51$ at the profit-maximizing quantity.

::: solution

$(P - ATC) \times Q = (85 - 51) \times 25 = 850$ coins.

:::

d\) There are no externalities. Mark the socially efficient quantity and shade the deadweight loss.

::: solution

The efficient quantity is where demand crosses $MC$: $110 - Q = 10 + 2Q$, so $Q = 33\frac{1}{3}$. At 25 cauldrons the price is 85 and the marginal cost is 60, so the deadweight loss is the triangle between demand and $MC$ from 25 to $33\frac{1}{3}$ (about 104 coins).

:::

Now suppose the Ministry taxes every cauldron 20 coins, so marginal cost rises: $MC = 30 + 2Q$.

e\) What quantity and price maximize the firm’s profit after the new cost?

::: solution

$110 - 2Q = 30 + 2Q$, so $80 = 4Q$ and $Q = 20$. The price is $P = 110 - 20 = 90$.

:::

f\) Calculate the firm’s maximal profit if $ATC = 70$ at the new quantity.

::: solution

$(90 - 70) \times 20 = 400$ coins, down from 850.

:::

g\) How much does the price rise? Is that more or less than the tax?

::: solution

The price rises by 5, from 85 to 90: a quarter of the 20-coin tax. The Witching Hour pays the rest out of its profit. Compare Vignette E2, where in the long run the competitive price rose by the whole tax.

:::
